sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. observational random design on \([0,1]^d\) with an unknown Lebesgue density satisfying only \(f_{-}\leq f_P\leq f_{+}\).
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes \(O=(X,A,Y)\) with bounded potential outcomes.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is binary, consistent, and conditionally exchangeable given \(X\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The propensity and control regression may be estimated at their known H\"older indices inside the local \(R\)-construction. The design density is never estimated, and no density smoothness or density-estimation rate is imposed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 bounds pointwise CATE risk at the three-term optimized rate under its stated local covariate-law estimation condition.
Theorem 1 gives same-sample stabilized empirical-HOIF bias, variance \(O(n^{-1}+k n^{-2})\), and a Gaussian limit for global bilinear forms when \(k\lesssim n/(\log n)^3\).
The empirical-HOIF construction replaces density estimation by an inverse sample Gram computed on an independent sample under a below-rank restriction.
Section 2, Theorem 2.1 gives a finite two-scale close-pair upper bound for homoskedastic variance and a separate density-regular HOIF comparison.
The pointwise variance theorem analyzes a local-polynomial pairwise-difference \(U\)-statistic under random design.
The paper establishes doubly robust confidence bands in a first-order local-smoothing regime.

body.tldr: A single bounded local \(R\)-estimator is to attain the KBRW pointwise-CATE benchmark on an explicitly restricted fixed positive two-sided covariate-density-band class. On \(G_n\), a same-sample M\"obius-stabilized empirical local Gram removes density estimation; on \(P_n\), a finite-order signed multiresolution close-pair correction handles rank stress. The correction order and asymmetric validity frontier are derived objects, with a required nonempty open extension beyond the banked \(0<\beta<\alpha\leq1\) wedge. Within this fixed-band class, the estimator avoids the density-estimation or density-ratio condition used by the KBRW upper theorem at the same objective; no weakening, tightening, or inclusion relation between theorem classes is claimed.

project_justification.gap: KBRW publish the sharp pointwise-CATE benchmark and an upper theorem with a local covariate-law condition. It is unresolved whether that same three-term objective is attainable without density estimation or a density-ratio condition after explicitly restricting attention to laws with a fixed positive two-sided density band. Existing density-free empirical HOIF results are global and rank-limited, while close-pair results target noncausal variance functionals.
project_justification.niche: The explicitly restricted fixed positive-band class supplies local mass but no smooth density model. Within that class, the optimizer reveals two complementary obstacles: same-sample inverse-Gram dependence below local rank and sparse collision geometry above it. This restriction is not asserted to weaken, tighten, or contain the KBRW theorem class.
project_justification.fill: On the fixed positive-band class, the project derives both branch constructions, proves the KBRW three-term risk envelope without density estimation, a density-ratio condition, or logarithmic loss, extends the close-pair smoothness region, and combines the branches through the deterministic exhaustive selector \((G_n,P_n)\) with bounded fallbacks.

body.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) define the destination benchmark and local higher-order \(R\)-learner, and their upper theorem uses a local covariate-law estimation condition. The present result uses their objective as a benchmark and, on the explicitly restricted fixed positive-band class, seeks attainment without density estimation or a density-ratio condition; it makes no weakening, tightening, or inclusion claim about the two theorem classes. Liu, Li, Gu, and Liu (2026) provide the M\"obius, Neumann-remainder, and graph-counting method adapted on the rank-feasible branch, but their target is a global bilinear form. Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins (2017) establish the independent empirical-Gram ancestor. Dobriban, Mukherjee, Robins, and Wang (2026, Section 2, Theorem 2.1) motivate the two-regime synthesis and projected-pair screening for homoskedastic variance. Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han (2020) supply the closest pairwise-difference \(U\)-statistic analysis. Robins et al. (2008, 2017) inform finite higher-order correction, without delivering the localized causal residual algebra. Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017) concern first-order CATE inference and are not a theorem-level target here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The rank-stressed theorem rests on solving the open moment-cancellation and Hoeffding-accounting problem in \(\mathrm{oeq:multiresolution\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}frontier}\). A singular local empirical Gram only triggers a bounded estimator fallback; it is not evidence for an all-estimator lower bound. The KBRW support-hole fuzzy-hypothesis construction is outside the fixed-positive-band class and is not used for a converse.
body.honest_scope: Identification and the oracle local-regression reduction are standard. The new theorem-level work is the two upper-bound branches and their exact deterministic stitching. The finite multiresolution order, signed weights, and maximal smoothness region are deliberately left for derivation rather than assumed. No density-induced slowdown, new minimax lower bound, adaptive unknown-smoothness guarantee, or elbow-uniform confidence interval is claimed.
